calls.head: The Panthers’ power play has a target
calls.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is the league’s worst, and the Panthers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight. The Panthers draw a lot of penalties, so their power play should get its chances.
calls.call: The Panthers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.4 expected goals per 60.

calls.head: The Panthers shut down the dangerous stuff, the Canucks don’t
calls.body: On preventing dangerous shots, Florida is one of the league’s best, but Vancouver is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. The more dangerous chances should come at the Canucks’ net.
calls.call: The Panthers prevent dangerous shots better than the Canucks do.

surprises.head: Florida hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Florida is one of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 77 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 156 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 500 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: A natural hat trick for Brady Tkachuk
paras: Liam Öhgren got the scoring started for the Canucks early in the first, and Elias Pettersson (#25) stretched the lead to 2-0 late in the period. Brady Tkachuk cut Vancouver’s lead to 2-1 midway through the third. With the goalie pulled and 13 seconds left, Brady Tkachuk scored again to tie it 2-2. Brady Tkachuk completed a natural hat trick to win it less than three minutes into overtime. It was his second straight hat trick. The Canucks’ Filip Chytil played his first game of the season, after missing the first eight, and picked up an assist.

The Panthers outshot the Canucks 39-17, but the Canucks’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Akira Schmid made 15 saves for the Panthers, and Leevi Meriläinen stopped 36 of 39 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Aaron Ekblad had the best night of anyone, even with Brady Tkachuk’s hat trick in the game. The Cats moved to 4-2-2, fourth in the Atlantic, while the Canucks dropped to 2-6-1, sixth in the Pacific.
